tone_statements.citation: Nishida, Fuminobu (西田文信). 2017. ブータン王国の諸言語について －言語多様性の現状と課題－ [On the languages of the Kingdom of Bhutan: the current state and issues of linguistic diversity]. Handout (席上配布資料) for the 43rd Yunnan Konwakai (第43回雲南懇話会), Tokyo, December 2017. 6 pp. (A revised version focused on Lhokpu appeared as ヒマラヤ学誌 20: 63-74, 2019.)
tone_statements.quote: ・超分節要素は，高低アクセントか声調かで研究者 により解釈が異なるが，Tshangla，Lepcha 以外の諸言語には少なくとも高低アクセントが存在することが確認されている。また，２音節語の単音節化が広くみられる。
tone_statements.translation: As for suprasegmentals, researchers differ in interpreting them as pitch (high-low) accent or as tone, but it has been confirmed that at least a pitch accent exists in the languages other than Tshangla and Lepcha. Monosyllabification of disyllabic words is also widely observed.
tone_statements.locator: p. 4, section 1(4)② 'ブータン諸語に特徴的なこと' > '類似現象の例' (areal features list); Lakha named in the language list p. 1, section 1(1)
tone_statements.summary: Areal claim only: Lakha, like all Bhutanese languages except Tshangla and Lepcha, has at least a two-way high/low pitch (accent) contrast; whether it is a pitch accent or a tone system is left open; no number of tones, TBU or stress interaction given for Lakha.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: an introduction to the family of languages derived from Old Tibetan. Villejuif: LACITO Publications. 1151 pp.
sources.note: Nothing Lakha-specific. Lakha = 'Säphuk pastoralists' dialect', S-section group 73 (pp. 555-556, 559-561): 'There is little available information and a general survey is needed about these three pastoralist dialects'; sec. 9.7.6 p. 561: S-section dialects 'generally have two distinctive pitch tones' but 'We lack data about the pastoralists' dialects'. Family-level sec. 7.3.3 Stress / 7.3.4 Prosodic patterns (pp. 241-243): trochaic strong-weak pattern 'attested in most dialects with a tonal distinction, such as Kham, Dzongkha and Sherpa' -- not stated for Lakha.

sources.citation: van Driem, George. 2007. South Asia and the Middle East. In C. Moseley (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages, 283-348. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 314, 334: Brokpas of Säphu Geo in Wangdi Phodr'a speak 'Lakha.. or Tshangkha', c. 8,000 speakers, Central Bodish, endangered.
sources.venue: Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages
